result.title: Geometric Parrots: Rule Absence vs. Rule Fragility in Spatial and Physical Reasoning for Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer many geometric and physical reasoning questions correctly, yet still behave inconsistently in interaction, for example, abandoning a correct answer when confronted with a confident but incorrect user assertion. Standard single-turn accuracy cannot distinguish such capitulations from beneficial corrections because it scores each response in isolation. We introduce GRIP, a controlled benchmark with 34 procedurally generated reasoning domains, 100,000 images, and 600,000 questions spanning geometric, spatial, visual, and physical reasoning. Each scene is generated by deterministic code, and every answer is derived directly from the underlying scene state, providing exact ground truth without human annotation. On GRIP, we propose Dual-Loop Evaluation. A closed loop probes each image with a five-step compositional question ladder to localize where reasoning fails. An open loop then re-elicits the model's answer under controlled challenges, including peer-model responses and unsupported user assertions. Because ground truth is known exactly, answer changes can be signed as corrections (wrong-to-right) or capitulations (right-to-wrong), separating two failure modes: rule absence and rule fragility. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/bilaljawaid980/GRIP-Benchmark, with further details at https://bilaljawaid980.github.io/grip-benchmark/.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GRIP，一个由确定性代码程序化生成场景与精确标注的几何、空间、视觉与物理推理基准（34 个域、10 万图、60 万问答），并设计「双环评估」：闭环用五步组合式问题阶梯定位推理失败环节，开环在同伴模型回答或无依据的用户断言下重新诱答，从而把答案变化区分为纠正与屈服，以分离「规则缺失」与「规则脆弱」两种失败模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接诊断 VLM 在几何与空间推理上是否真正依赖视觉证据，其可控挑战下的答案翻转与组合式阶梯，可供核查模型内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉信息、以及答案对视觉旁路与外部提示的依赖程度。
